runs.t: The Pareto principle is a heuristic that a minority of causes often account for a majority of outcomes. The familiar 80/20 ratio is illustrative, not a guaranteed mathematical law.

Rank performance bottlenecks, incident sources, customer complaints or feature adoption using real data. Target high-impact causes first, then remeasure because distributions evolve as constraints are removed.
If three endpoints account for most slow requests, optimizing those may help users more than optimizing dozens of low-traffic handlers. Validate against severity, not just frequency.
Rare events can be catastrophic despite low volume; security and compliance cannot be prioritized by frequency alone. Do not manufacture an 80/20 result from arbitrary grouping.
